article_notes: Central Poland: 58 dogs with B. canis babesiosis (smear, confirmed by 18S PCR; 30 sequenced as B. canis genotype 2), samples via a diagnostic laboratory; CBC available for 41 and biochemistry for 37. The authors built three symptom severity classes (anaemia by RBC, hepatic by AST/ALT, renal by urea; 0/1/2; Table 2, ANOVA) and an overall babesiosis severity level 1-3 (mild n=10, moderate n=11, severe n=20). Table 2 markers are largely the defining variables. The main host factor tested is D. repens co-infection (52/58 dogs) against the severity classes by log-linear analysis: no significant association. Table 1 (co-infected n=36/32 vs B. canis only n=5) and Table 3 (D. repens x severity class interaction ANOVAs) compare blood values between co-infection groups, not between severity groups: listed in not_extracted. Only 5 dogs had B. canis alone. Skipped: D. repens prevalence babesiosis vs healthy dogs (1).

severity_definitions.label: anaemia severity class 2 (severe) vs class 1 (mild) vs class 0 (normal)
severity_definitions.definition: Score by RBC count: 0 = 5.5-8.0 T/l, 1 = 4.5-5.5 T/l, 2 = below 4.5 T/l. Class 0 n=15, class 1 n=14, class 2 n=12.
severity_definitions.quote: severity of anemia (severity score 0- RBC counts within normal range 5.5–8.0 T/l; severity score 1- RBC counts in a range 4.5–5.5 T/l; severity score 2- RBC below 4.5 T/l)

severity_definitions.label: hepatic dysfunction class 2 (hepatic failure) vs class 1 (abnormal) vs class 0 (normal)
severity_definitions.definition: AST and ALT (with accompanying ALP) within reference range (0), above it up to 100 U/l (1), or above 100 U/l (2). Class 0 n=5, class 1 n=22, class 2 n=10.
severity_definitions.quote: hepatic dysfunction parameters (measures of enzymes activity [based on reference values for AST – aspartate aminotransferase and ALT- alanine aminotransferase; with accompanying ALP – alkaline phosphatase] within, above (up to 100 U/l) and profoundly above (>100 U/l) the normal range, representing scores of 0, 1 and 2, respectively, Table 2)

severity_definitions.label: renal dysfunction class 2 vs class 1 vs class 0
severity_definitions.definition: Serum urea within reference range (0), above it up to 100 mg/dl (1), or above 100 mg/dl (2). Class 0 n=25, class 1 n=7, class 2 n=5.
severity_definitions.quote: renal dysfunction parameters (based on reference values for serum urea within, above (up to 100 mg/dl) and profoundly above (>100 mg/dl) the normal range, representing severity scores of 0, 1 and 2, respectively, Table 2)

severity_definitions.label: severe (level 3) vs moderate (level 2) vs mild (level 1) babesiosis
severity_definitions.definition: Level 3: any of anaemia, hepatic or renal dysfunction at score 2 (n=20); level 2: more than one dysfunction at score 1 (n=11); level 1: only one group of symptoms, mainly mild anaemia and thrombocytopenia (n=10).
severity_definitions.quote: Then all dogs with any of these three general symptoms classified as ‘severity score 2’ were assigned to group 3 (severe babesiosis, severity level 3, n = 20)
